newsitem.title: USA: Florida house panel rebuffs nudist ban.
newsitem.headline: Florida house panel rebuffs nudist ban.

text.p: A proposal to outlaw nude sunbathing on some Florida beaches was nipped in the bud on Tuesday by lawmakers saying it would hurt tourism.
By a 6-3 margin, a House committee defied its chairman's wishes and defeated a measure that would have made it illegal to be seen naked in public at any of the state's 10 federal parks.
The proposal hit organised opposition not only from nudists' rights groups but from South Florida lawmakers and tourism officials.
Especially hard hit would be the state's European market, where travellers as a group are more accustomed to nude sunbathing then their U.S. counterparts.

Representative Randy Ball, R-Mims, chairman of the House Crime and Punishment Committee, said he filed the bill on the urging of constituents in Titusville, who complained about nude sunbathers at Canaveral National Seashore, a 25-mile (40-km) stretch of beach along Florida's Atlantic coast.
Ball said nudists who had kept to a remote section of the park were now "ranging" the entire beach, shocking families and other "textile dependent" sunbathers.
"A lot of you are getting calls from South Florida saying this bill is specifically prohibiting nudity on their beaches," Ball said. "It is not. It is shutting down none of their beaches."
But despite Ball's assurances, opponents said the bill would set a dangerous precedent and make it easier for lawmakers to later expand the prohibition to other beaches.

Nudist advocates hailed the vote, saying nudists did a good job of policing themselves. Supporters of the ban said they would look for federal help to take back beaches they say they are being driven from by nude sunbathers.
A similar bill is pending action in the Florida Senate, but without a House companion, it will have a considerably more difficult time passing both chambers.
